blocks.raw: <Tip>Remember the rule: High water absorption + humid or wet exposure = poor durability. Limestone and travertine (high absorption) fail in tropical Philippines without protection; granite (low absorption) performs well.</Tip>

blocks.raw:
<WikiMistakeCard
  mistake="Assuming harder stone (higher Mohs number) is always stronger (higher compressive strength)"
  correction="Mohs hardness and compressive strength are different properties. A material can be hard but weak (e.g., some slate). Marble (Mohs 3—4) may have lower hardness but higher compressive strength than some sandstones. Always check both properties for design."
  context="Designers sometimes select stone based on hardness alone, overlooking compressive strength and absorption issues." />

props.mistake: Assuming harder stone (higher Mohs number) is always stronger (higher compressive strength)
props.correction: Mohs hardness and compressive strength are different properties. A material can be hard but weak (e.g., some slate). Marble (Mohs 3—4) may have lower hardness but higher compressive strength than some sandstones. Always check both properties for design.
props.context: Designers sometimes select stone based on hardness alone, overlooking compressive strength and absorption issues.
